data.title: SEO
data.tagline: SEO is ongoing work that helps search engines understand, discover, and present web content.
data.learningOutcome: You can ask for real, clearly structured, accessible content and distinguish SEO fundamentals from a ranking promise.
data.description: A help article that truly answers a question with clear headings, body structure, and reachable links is easier for search systems to understand; product pages also need accessible content and links. SEO improves the conditions for understanding and presentation, not a guarantee of a particular keyword rank.

learning.assumes: You have used a search engine to find an answer or published a page others need to find through a link.
learning.outcome: You can ask for real, clearly structured, accessible content and distinguish SEO fundamentals from a ranking promise.

explanation.title: Content answers a real question first
explanation.text: A page needs useful, accurate content. Its title and sections tell people and search systems what it solves; keyword stuffing or vague promotion cannot replace an answer.

explanation.title: Crawlers read pages through links and HTML
explanation.text: Search engines follow links to discover pages and read title, meta description, heading structure, and image alt attributes. Pure client-rendered apps with empty initial HTML may hide content from crawlers.

explanation.title: AI-generated pages often need SEO polish
explanation.text: AI often misses unique titles and meta descriptions, single-h1 hierarchy, image alt text, and semantic HTML (article, nav, main). Check and fix these basics before launching.

data.boundary: SEO is neither buying rank nor changing a few keywords. Results depend on query intent, competition, quality, and system judgment among other factors. Clear content and technical accessibility are necessary work but cannot promise traffic or position.

lessonPractice.title: After an old help page is redesigned, visitors from its existing link still need a destination. What approach fits best?

options.label: Redirect the old URL to the new page that truly corresponds to its content, then check both old and new link behavior
options.feedback: Correct. Visitors and search systems reach relevant replacement content instead of a dead end.

options.label: Delete the old page with no handling and let search engines update later
options.feedback: People following old links get an error page, harming usability and related signals.

options.label: Send every old page to the homepage regardless of what it covered
options.feedback: The home page may not answer the need expressed by the old link. Redirects should match real replacement content when possible.

data.agentPrompt: Check the SEO fundamentals of this help article: whether its title accurately answers the problem, headings are clear, and key content and links are accessible. Do not promise rankings. Afterward, open it in a normal browser and check that old links reach corresponding content.
